claim: A large collection of Minos-Mediated Integration Cassettes (MiMICs) contain two phiC31 recombinase target sites.
source: Previously, we described a large collection of Minos-Mediated Integration Cassettes (MiMICs) that contain two phiC31 recombinase target sites and allow the generation of a new exon that encodes a protein tag when the MiMIC is inserted in a codon intron (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015).

claim: MiMICs allow the generation of a new exon that encodes a protein tag when inserted in a codon intron.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015).

claim: Modified genes with MiMIC insertions permit assessment of protein expression pattern.
source: These modified genes permit numerous applications including assessment of protein expression pattern, identification of protein interaction partners by immunoprecipitation followed by mass spec, and reversible removal of the tagged protein in any tissue.
evidence: This claim is based on the described capabilities of the modified genes in the manuscript.

claim: A simple and reliable genetic strategy was developed to tag genes/proteins that contain MiMIC insertions using an integrated exon encoding GFP flanked by FRT sequences.

claim: Generating transgenic animals with epitope tags fused to genes at their normal genomic location is one of the most powerful techniques for characterizing gene function.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Ross-Macdonald et al., 1999; Morin et al., 2001; Skarnes et al., 2004).

claim: Tagged proteins permit determination of protein localization in vivo.
